headline: Senate rejected a resolution that would have canceled the Education Department rule creating the SAVE student loan repayment plan.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Department of Education rule published on July 10, 2023. That rule created a new income-driven repayment plan for federal student loans called the Saving on a Valuable Education (SAVE) plan. If adopted, the rule would have had no legal effect. Under that law, the department also generally could not issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Federal student loan borrowers with Direct Loans or FFEL loans
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost access to the SAVE plan as a repayment option tied to their income.
It would have been barred from carrying out the SAVE plan rule or issuing a substantially similar one without action by Congress.
